13: # Goal Budget and Handoff
14: 
15: ## 1. OVERVIEW
16: 
17: Use the packet report to check a top-level goal or phase parent. Keep every completion criterion when cutting an over-budget parent. Section 2 is the one rule for which goals carry the cap, section 3 the one full cut order and section 4 the one full rule for what a parent goal sent in chat contains. Other documents point here rather than restating them.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 2. MEASURE THE DURABLE SLICE
22: 
23: Run this command from the repository root:
24: 
25: ```bash
26: node .skilled/hooks/goal/bin/goal.cjs packet <packet> --workspace <repo root>
27: ```
28: 
29: Replace the placeholders with the packet path and repository root. Read `packet_durable_chars` and `packet_budget` in the output. The count covers text after the closing frontmatter fence and before the log anchor. Anchors and comments inside that range count. The manifest sets the limit to 4,000 characters for top-level packets and phase parents. A count of 4,000 is within budget. A larger count reports `packet_budget=over`. ([manifest, lines 24 to 28](../../../system-spec-kit/templates/spec-kit-docs.json))
30: 
31: The packet command prints the count and budget state with the other packet fields. ([packet output, lines 205 to 218](../../../../hooks/goal/bin/goal.cjs)) The shared module measures the durable slice from the frontmatter boundary to the log anchor. ([slice measurement, lines 57 to 68](../../../../hooks/goal/lib/goal-slice.cjs))
32: 
33: The cap applies to a top-level packet and to any folder that is itself a phase parent, meaning it has phase children or its `spec.md` declares the phase level, even when that folder sits inside another packet. Only a phase child that is not itself a phase parent is exempt, and its packet report reads `packet_budget=unknown`. `goal.cjs packet`, `check-goal.cjs` and `validate.sh` draw this same line. An applicable goal can also report `unknown` if the budget manifest is missing or invalid. Treat that result as unverified and resolve the manifest issue before judging the goal. ([budget resolution, lines 288 to 307](../../../../hooks/goal/lib/goal-slice.cjs) and [applicability and state, lines 400 to 415](../../../../hooks/goal/lib/goal-slice.cjs))
34: 
35: ---
36: 
37: ## 3. CUT IN THIS ORDER
38: 
39: When a parent exceeds 4,000 characters, cut in this order and rerun the packet command after the cuts.
40: 
41: 1. Check the frontmatter first. It is bookkeeping outside the measured slice, so changing it does not lower `packet_durable_chars`.
42: 2. Check the log next. It is outside the durable directive and the measured slice, so changing it does not lower `packet_durable_chars`.
43: 3. Remove author instructions an older template left above the log: a blockquote under the title, an `Operator copy` section and a criteria introduction. First move any packet-specific sentence written under those headings into the objective or a decision.
44: 4. Remove parent text that restates a child's goal. The binding makes the child goal authoritative for its phase.
45: 5. Shorten decision prose to the choice a later author must honor. Put the argument in the decision record.
46: 6. Shorten criterion wording only as needed. Keep the same number of criteria and make each one checkable, following [authoring standards, section 4](authoring-standards.md). If the goal repeats these criteria in its objective, update that copy to match.
47: 
48: If the parent still exceeds the limit after those cuts, split the packet into separate goals. Never remove a criterion to fit the budget.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## 4. WHAT A PARENT GOAL SENT IN CHAT CONTAINS
53: 
54: Send a parent goal in chat only as the `chat_slice` that `goal.cjs packet` prints, and only when the same report shows `packet_budget=ok`. Never paste the file, a summary of it or any other text. ([packet output, lines 205 to 218](../../../../hooks/goal/bin/goal.cjs))
55: 
56: A parent goal sent in chat never contains:
57: 
58: - Frontmatter
59: - HTML comments, which include every anchor marker and template marker
60: - `---` dividers
61: - Heading section numbers
62: - Author instructions, meaning template text that tells a writer how to fill, cut or resend the file
63: 
64: The chat slice removes the first four. ([chat rendering, lines 78 to 85](../../../../hooks/goal/lib/goal-slice.cjs)) The current templates carry no author instructions above the log, so a goal filled from them sends none. What stays is the title, the objective, the decision table, the binding table with its Read, Precedence and Stop rules, and the completion criteria.
65: 
66: The 4,000-character limit is measured on the durable slice, with comments and anchors counted. `validate.sh`, `check-goal.cjs` and `goal.cjs packet` all measure that text. The chat slice only removes text from the durable slice, so a parent at `packet_budget=ok` never sends more than 4,000 characters. When the report shows `over`, cut the file in the section 3 order and measure again. Never truncate the chat slice to fit. When a top-level goal or phase parent shows `unknown`, fix the manifest first.
67: 
68: A goal filled from an older template can still carry a blockquote under its title, an `Operator copy` section or a criteria introduction. `AGENTS.md` overrides any resend wording in them. Remove them the next time the parent is amended or cut, as section 3 step 3 says.
69: 
70: On Claude Code, send the `chat_slice` inside one fenced code block that holds the slice and nothing else. The operator sets the goal by typing the native `/goal` command, and the block gives them a copy button and byte-exact text that markdown rendering cannot alter. Open it with a plain `text` fence and put no prose inside it. Make the fence longer than the longest run of backticks in the slice, so a slice that holds three backticks opens with four or more backticks or with `~~~`. The fence is presentation around the slice and adds no content, so every rule above still holds for what sits inside it.
71: 
72: The `objective_slice` is a different projection, assembled for a runtime bind, and it is never pasted in chat. It starts with a packet pointer and adds standard binding and precedence text when the goal has a binding anchor. It then copies checked completion criteria. It does not contain the authored objective or decision table. ([objective projection, lines 112 to 124](../../../../hooks/goal/lib/goal-slice.cjs))
73: 
74: After a parent goal changes, print the current packet report. This mode prints `chat_slice` and stops. The runtime that owns session state handles any later handoff. The mode does not change session state.
75: 
76: ---
77: 
78: ## 5. RUNTIME HANDOFF MATRIX
79: 
80: The table records each runtime's role and what the repository evidence can establish. This mode always stops after it prints `chat_slice`.
81: 
82: | Runtime | Surface role | Evidence limit |
83: |---|---|---|
84: | Claude Code | Uses the native host goal command. The spec-kit workflow hands the stripped durable slice to the operator as one fenced code block that holds the slice and nothing else. | Repository documentation records operator confirmation. Recheck host behavior in a live Claude Code session. ([goal hooks README, lines 81 to 84](../../../../hooks/goal/README.md) and [goal plugin, lines 159 to 160](../../../../hooks/goal/goal-plugin.md)) |
85: | Codex | Uses the native host goal command and the same operator handoff as Claude Code, without the fenced block, which is a Claude Code rule. | Repository documentation records operator confirmation. Recheck host behavior in a live Codex session. ([goal hooks README, lines 81 to 84](../../../../hooks/goal/README.md) and [goal plugin, lines 159 to 160](../../../../hooks/goal/goal-plugin.md)) |
86: | OpenCode | A native plugin owns per-session goal files and provides `/goal-opencode` tools. | The repository documents the plugin and command. A live OpenCode session confirms host loading. ([goal hooks README, lines 75 and 80](../../../../hooks/goal/README.md) and [goal plugin, lines 155 and 166](../../../../hooks/goal/goal-plugin.md)) |
87: | Pi | A native session-bound extension registers `/goal-pi` and supplies the runtime session identity. | The repository documents extension registration. A live Pi session confirms host loading. ([goal hooks README, lines 75 and 77](../../../../hooks/goal/README.md) and [goal plugin, lines 156 and 168](../../../../hooks/goal/goal-plugin.md)) |
88: | Cursor | The prompt command reads a packet with `/goal-cursor packet <path>`. `packet-log` is a separate append action. | The read command needs no session identity. The hook's model visibility is recorded evidence, not an end-to-end guarantee. ([goal hooks README, lines 75 and 78](../../../../hooks/goal/README.md) and [Cursor command, lines 10 and 14 to 19](../../../../../.cursor/commands/goal-cursor.md)) |
89: | Devin | Hooks inject goal context. The repository exposes no Devin prompt-command surface. | The repository documents hook wiring. A live Devin session is needed to confirm host delivery. ([goal hooks README, lines 75 and 79](../../../../hooks/goal/README.md) and [goal plugin, lines 158 and 162 to 168](../../../../hooks/goal/goal-plugin.md)) |
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## 6. FIXED TEMPLATE COST
94: 
95: Measured on the unfilled blocks, the fixed text costs 1,624 durable characters for a phase parent, 1,004 for a top-level goal and 956 for a phase child. Most of that is placeholders and, for a parent, the binding rules. A live packet records its own count in its log, not here.
96: 
97: The fixed-text cost is an authoring constraint. If a goal still cannot meet the contract after the section 3 cuts, raise the gap to system-spec-kit as an amendment.

1: ---
2: title: "Parent and Nested Goal Authoring"
3: description: "Ordered workflows for packet goals, phase-parent bindings, nested child goals, retrofit, phase-add and amendments."
4: trigger_phrases:
5:   - "phase-parent goal"
6:   - "nested child goal"
7:   - "goal retrofit"
8:   - "phase-add binding"
9:   - "parent goal amendment"
10: importance_tier: important
11: contextType: implementation
12: version: 1.2.0.0
13: ---
14: # Parent and Nested Goal Authoring
15: 
16: ---
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW AND SOURCE CHECK
19: 
20: Use these workflows only after the packet and its phase structure exist. Read [`authoring-standards.md`](authoring-standards.md) and [`goal-exemplars.md`](../assets/goal-exemplars.md) before drafting. Start from the template for the goal's kind: [`goal-top-level-template.md`](../assets/goal-top-level-template.md), [`goal-phase-parent-template.md`](../assets/goal-phase-parent-template.md) or [`goal-phase-child-template.md`](../assets/goal-phase-child-template.md). Each is a checked copy of system-spec-kit's [goal template](../../../system-spec-kit/templates/addons/goal.md.tmpl), which owns the file structure.
21: 
22: Classify the target before writing. A top-level packet has its own specification and no parent packet spec. A phase parent has direct numbered phase-child folders. A nested child has a parent folder that contains `spec.md`.
23: 
24: Read the target's own `spec.md` and `acceptance-criteria.md`. For a phase parent, also read its Phase Documentation Map. For a nested child, use only that child's specification and acceptance criteria for its phase goal. Stop if a required source is missing or if the sources conflict. Name the conflict instead of choosing a truth silently.
25: 
26: Use [`create.sh`](../../../system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh) when scaffolding a packet with its other documents, and fill the `goal.md` it writes. For an existing packet or a missing goal, copy the block between the markers of the matching asset template. Never create or edit `goal.md.tmpl` in this mode.
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ## 2. TOP-LEVEL GOAL
31: 
32: 1. Read the packet's own `spec.md` and `acceptance-criteria.md`. Use the specification for the purpose and frozen decisions. Use the acceptance criteria for the completion checks. Resolve any contradiction before writing.
33: 2. If the packet already has `goal.md`, revise that file through its existing structure. If it has no goal, copy the template block from [`goal-top-level-template.md`](../assets/goal-top-level-template.md) into the packet directory as `goal.md`.
34: 3. Write one objective sentence that states the packet's purpose. Record decisions that later work must honor. Add three to seven self-contained completion criteria based on the acceptance criteria. Repeat those criteria verbatim in the evaluator-facing objective text required by the goal contract.
35: 4. Keep progress and temporary findings below the goal's log heading. A top-level goal has no binding section.
36: 
37: Verify the packet from the repository root:
38: 
39: ```bash
40: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh <packet> --strict
41: node .skilled/hooks/goal/bin/goal.cjs packet <packet> --workspace "$PWD"
42: ```
43: 
44: Read both outputs. Require `RESULT: PASSED` from strict validation. Confirm the goal packet command reports `packet_budget=ok` and that the objective and criteria match the packet's own sources.
45: 
46: ---
47: 
48: ## 3. PHASE-PARENT GOAL
49: 
50: A phase-parent binding is complete only when the map and direct child folders agree. The validator checks targets that appear in the binding table. It does not detect a missing row, compare the map with the folders or prove that every phase is listed. Use the [goal validator](../../../system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/validation/spec-doc-structure.ts) as a target check, not as a completeness check.
51: 
52: 1. Read the phase parent's `spec.md`, its `acceptance-criteria.md` when present and the complete Phase Documentation Map. Record each direct phase folder named by the map.
53: 2. List every direct child directory whose name matches `NNN-slug/`. Compare the exact folder-name set with the map's folder set before writing the goal. Do not compare only the counts.
54: 3. **STOP** if a map row has no matching directory, a directory has no map row or a folder name is ambiguous. Report the exact map and disk entries that differ. Reconcile the Phase Documentation Map first, then restart this workflow. Never infer a folder name or guess a missing binding row.
55: 4. Check that each child folder has its own `spec.md` and `acceptance-criteria.md`. Stop if either source is missing. Derive the parent's objective and criteria from the parent-level sources. Do not copy phase-local detail into the parent as a substitute for parent criteria.
56: 5. If the parent has no `goal.md`, copy the template block from [`goal-phase-parent-template.md`](../assets/goal-phase-parent-template.md). If it already has a goal, revise it through its existing structure. Preserve the template's binding and precedence text.
57: 6. Write exactly one table row for each direct phase-child directory. The target cell must be a backticked path in the form `NNN-slug/goal.md`, relative to the phase parent. For example:
58: 
59: | Phase | Goal document |
60: |---|---|
61: | source audit | `001-source-audit/goal.md` |
62: 
63: Do not add a row for a phase-map entry without a matching directory. Do not omit a directory because it lacks a child goal yet. The phase parent's criteria describe parent outcomes and remain checkable without opening another file.
64: 
65: Verify from the repository root. Compare the map folder set, the direct-child directory set and the binding target set by name. Confirm each target exists. Then validate recursively and measure the parent goal:
66: 
67: ```bash
68: find <packet> -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name '[0-9][0-9][0-9]-*' -print | sort
69: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh <packet> --recursive --strict
70: node .skilled/hooks/goal/bin/goal.cjs packet <packet> --workspace "$PWD"
71: ```
72: 
73: The strict validator checks each listed target but does not prove row completeness. Your set comparison is a separate required check. Require `RESULT: PASSED` and `packet_budget=ok`.
74: 
75: ---
76: 
77: ## 4. NESTED CHILD GOAL
78: 
79: 1. Read the child's own `spec.md` and `acceptance-criteria.md`. Use its phase objective, frozen choices and phase-local criteria. Do not derive the child goal from a parent summary or another phase's criteria.
80: 2. Fill the child's scaffolded `goal.md`, or copy the template block from [`goal-phase-child-template.md`](../assets/goal-phase-child-template.md) when it has none. Fill the objective, decisions and three to seven checkable criteria. Repeat those criteria verbatim in the evaluator-facing objective text required by the goal contract.
81: 3. Keep the criteria phase-local. A nested child goal has no binding section. The parent goal binds the child.
82: 
83: Verify the child and the absence of a binding section:
84: 
85: ```bash
86: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh <child> --strict
87: ! grep -q '<!-- ANCHOR:binding -->' <child>/goal.md
88: ```
89: 
90: Require `RESULT: PASSED`. Confirm every child criterion traces to that child's own acceptance criteria and that the goal has no binding block.
91: 
92: ---
93: 
94: ## 5. RETROFIT AND PHASE-ADD
95: 
96: ### Retrofit a missing goal
97: 
98: Treat adding a goal to an existing packet that has none as its own operation. First confirm the packet exists, its role is clear and its source documents are present. Do not call this operation when a goal already exists. Revise that file instead.
99: 
100: `create.sh --phase --with-goal` writes goals through the child document contract. Its phase-parent path renders the lean parent specification separately and does not create a parent `goal.md`. For that missing parent, copy the template block from [`goal-phase-parent-template.md`](../assets/goal-phase-parent-template.md) into the packet directory as `goal.md`.
101: 
102: Fill it from the parent's sources and complete its binding table using the phase-parent workflow. For a non-phase packet, use [`goal-top-level-template.md`](../assets/goal-top-level-template.md) instead.
103:

8: # Create Packet Goals

12: ---
13: 
14: ## 1. WHEN TO USE
15: 
16: ### Activation Triggers
17: 
18: Use this packet to:
19: 
20: - Author or revise a top-level goal or phase-parent goal.
21: - Author or revise a nested phase-child goal.
22: - Add `goal.md` to an existing packet that has no goal.
23: - Add a binding row and matching child goal when someone adds a phase.
24: - Cut an over-budget parent goal without dropping a completion criterion.
25: - Print a parent goal's chat slice for the operator to set or resend.

27: 
28: Keyword triggers: `create packet goal`, `author goal.md`, `revise packet goal`, `phase parent goal`, `nested phase child goal`, `add a goal file`, `goal chat slice`, `/create:goal`.
29: 
30: ### When NOT to Use
31: 
32: - The target packet does not exist. Use system-spec-kit to create it first.
33: - The packet's phase structure is not established. Use system-spec-kit to plan the phases first.
34: - The request is to set, bind, inject or resend a session objective. Redirect it to the goal hooks or the host's native goal command.
35: - The request changes runtime goal behavior or system-spec-kit template tooling. Those owners remain outside this packet.
36: 
37: This packet authors files only. Its goal-file work does not change session state.
38: 
39: ---
40: 
41: ## 2. SMART ROUTING
42: 
43: The `sk-doc` hub routes goal-file authoring here: a request to author or revise a packet `goal.md` selects this packet through the hub's `sk-create-goal` mode signal.
44: A request to set, bind or resend a session objective is not file work, so the hub leaves it to the goal hooks.
45: 
46: An authoring or revision request loads [`references/parent-and-nested-goals.md`](references/parent-and-nested-goals.md) first, which holds the workflow for every goal kind.
47: The same request also loads [`references/authoring-standards.md`](references/authoring-standards.md), [`assets/goal-exemplars.md`](assets/goal-exemplars.md) and the template for the goal's kind.
48: A budget measurement or a chat-slice handoff loads [`references/budget-and-handoff.md`](references/budget-and-handoff.md).
49: 
50: Read [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) before selecting skill-local resources; open only the matched files.
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## 3. HOW IT WORKS
55: 
56: 1. Read the target packet's source specification and acceptance criteria. For a phase parent, read its phase map and inspect every direct phase-child directory on disk.
57: 2. Apply the four routing decisions in [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md). For top-level, phase-parent, nested-child, retrofit, phase-add and amendment work, load and follow [`references/parent-and-nested-goals.md`](references/parent-and-nested-goals.md). Identify which goal files to add or revise and whether a child change requires a parent amendment first.
58: 3. Start each goal from the template for its kind: [`goal-top-level-template.md`](assets/goal-top-level-template.md), [`goal-phase-parent-template.md`](assets/goal-phase-parent-template.md) or [`goal-phase-child-template.md`](assets/goal-phase-child-template.md).
59:    Each is a checked copy of system-spec-kit's [`goal.md.tmpl`](../../system-spec-kit/templates/addons/goal.md.tmpl) at that kind's level.
60:    Copy the block between its template markers into `goal.md`.
61:    When [`create.sh`](../../system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh) `--with-goal` has already scaffolded a child's `goal.md`, keep that file and fill it with the child template's guidance.
62:    Child scaffolding alone does not create its parent goal.
63: 4. Before filling the template, load [`authoring-standards.md`](references/authoring-standards.md) and [`goal-exemplars.md`](assets/goal-exemplars.md).
64:    Fill it with packet-specific content and apply both resources.
65:    Use three to seven self-contained completion criteria that can be checked without opening another file.
66:    Leave no template placeholders.
67:    Copy the criteria verbatim into the objective text required by the goal contract.
68: 5. For a phase parent, make the binding table match the filesystem. Add one row for each direct phase-child directory, with that child's goal document as the target. Keep the table only in the phase-parent goal.
69: 6. Keep the durable slice at or below 4,000 characters wherever the cap applies. Load [`references/budget-and-handoff.md`](references/budget-and-handoff.md): section 2 says which goals carry the cap and how to read the packet report, and section 3 is the cut order for a goal that runs over. Never remove a criterion or make one uncheckable.
70: 7. Before handing off any authored or revised goal, run `node .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-goal/scripts/check-goal.cjs <packet>` from the repository root and resolve each finding.
71:    A finding left open for any reason, an operator brief included, stops the run: report it, print no chat slice and end with `STATUS=FAIL`.
72:    To see which criteria may break rules 4 and 5 below, run the advisory lint `node .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-goal/scripts/lint-goal-criteria.cjs <packet>`.
73:    It always exits 0 and never blocks the handoff.
74: 8. Only after the checker passes, and after authoring or amending a parent goal, load [`references/budget-and-handoff.md`](references/budget-and-handoff.md) for the projection distinction and runtime matrix, then print its chat slice with `node .skilled/hooks/goal/bin/goal.cjs packet <packet> --workspace <root>`. The `chat_slice` is for the operator to set or resend. It is not a session bind.
75: 
76: ---
77: 
78: ## 4. RULES
79: 
80: ### ✅ ALWAYS
81: 
82: 1. Run the four pre-write decisions before changing a goal file.
83: 2. Derive each goal from the existing packet's source documents, not from a guessed or remembered summary.
84: 3. Start every goal from the asset template for its kind. Keep each template's fixed text identical to `goal.md.tmpl`. The parity test fails when they drift.
85: 4. Use three to seven self-contained criteria.
86: 5. Make each criterion checkable without opening another file.
87: 6. Remove every template placeholder.
88: 7. Preserve every criterion when cutting an over-budget parent.
89: 8. Compare each binding row with the direct phase-child directories on disk.
90: 9. Print the updated parent chat slice for the operator when parent goal content changes.
91: 
92: ### ⛔ NEVER
93: 
94: 1. Never change an asset template's fixed text or structure on its own. Change `goal.md.tmpl` through system-spec-kit, then carry its new fixed text into all three templates.
95: 2. Never modify system-spec-kit's template tooling or shared validator from this packet.
96: 3. Never bind a packet to a session, set or resend a session objective, inject runtime state or track whether an operator has set the goal.
97: 4. Never put a binding table in a top-level goal or a phase-child goal.
98: 5. Never omit a phase child from the parent's binding table or drop a completion criterion to meet the budget.
99: 
100: ### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
101: 
102: 1. The source documents disagree about a decision or criterion. They also must describe the same phase structure. Report any conflict instead of choosing a truth silently.
103: 2. A phase child is missing the source documents needed to author its goal.
104: 3. The parent phase map and child directories do not agree.
105: 4. A child change requires a parent decision or criterion amendment, but the request would leave the parent untouched.
106: 5. A parent cannot meet the durable budget without losing a criterion or making one unclear. Do not cut the criterion count. Ask whether the packet scope should be split.
107: 6. The request requires session-goal state or a change to a system-spec-kit-owned contract.
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: ## 5. REFERENCES
112: 
113: - [`references/parent-and-nested-goals.md`](references/parent-and-nested-goals.md) defines the top-level, phase-parent, child, retrofit, phase-add and amendment workflows.
114: - [`authoring-standards.md`](references/authoring-standards.md) gives the reader checks for goal content.
115: - [`references/budget-and-handoff.md`](references/budget-and-handoff.md) explains the durable budget, the one full cut order, what a parent goal sent in chat contains and the runtime handoff.
116: - [`goal-exemplars.md`](assets/goal-exemplars.md) records cited pass and failure examples.
117: - [`goal-top-level-template.md`](assets/goal-top-level-template.md), [`goal-phase-parent-template.md`](assets/goal-phase-parent-template.md) and [`goal-phase-child-template.md`](assets/goal-phase-child-template.md) are the blanks each goal kind is filled from.
118: - [`goal.md.tmpl`](../../system-spec-kit/templates/addons/goal.md.tmpl) is the system-spec-kit source the three templates copy.
119: - [`scripts/README.md`](scripts/README.md) describes the checker, the advisory criteria lint, its scorer and their tests.
120: - [`goal-set-string-playbook.md`](../../system-spec-kit/references/workflows/goal-set-string-playbook.md) documents the objective set string a runtime binds and when a changed goal is resent. The budget, the cut order and what a goal sent in chat contains are in `budget-and-handoff.md`.
121: - [`goal hooks README`](../../../hooks/goal/README.md) documents the runtime session-state boundary.
122: - [`goal.cjs`](../../../hooks/goal/bin/goal.cjs) prints a packet's file-derived slices without binding a session.
123: 
124: ---
125: 
126: ## 6. SUCCESS CRITERIA
127: 
128: - Every authored goal starts from the template for its kind, and all three templates match `goal.md.tmpl`.
129: - Every phase-parent binding row corresponds to a direct phase-child directory on disk. No child is omitted.
130: - Each goal has three to seven self-contained criteria. No template placeholders remain.
131: - Top-level and phase-parent durable slices meet the 4,000-character limit without losing a criterion.
132: - Print parent chat slices for the operator. Do not change session objectives or runtime state.
133: 
134: ---
135: 
136: ## 7. INTEGRATION POINTS
137: 
138: - **system-spec-kit:** Owns `goal.md.tmpl`, the source the three asset templates copy, and `create.sh --with-goal`, which scaffolds child goals with the same structure.
139: - **Goal hooks and host command:** Own session binding and objective delivery. This includes injection and resend tracking. This packet only authors the source file and prints its chat slice for the operator.
140: - **Command surface:** The intended entry point is `/create:goal`. The command itself lives outside this packet.
141: - **sk-doc:** Routes goal-file authoring to this packet.
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 8. RELATED RESOURCES
146: 
147: - [`README.md`](./README.md) is the short reader entry point.

54: ## 3. HOW IT WORKS
55: 
56: 1. Read the target packet's source specification and acceptance criteria. For a phase parent, read its phase map and inspect every direct phase-child directory on disk.
57: 2. Apply the four routing decisions in [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md). For top-level, phase-parent, nested-child, retrofit, phase-add and amendment work, load and follow [`references/parent-and-nested-goals.md`](references/parent-and-nested-goals.md). 58: 3. Start each goal from the template for its kind: [`goal-top-level-template.md`](assets/goal-top-level-template.md), [`goal-phase-parent-template.md`](assets/goal-phase-parent-template.md) or [`goal-phase-child-template.md`](assets/goal-phase-child-template.md).
59:    Each is a checked copy of system-spec-kit's [`goal.md.tmpl`](../../system-spec-kit/templates/addons/goal.md.tmpl) at that kind's level.

61:    When [`create.sh`](../../system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh) `--with-goal` has already scaffolded a child's `goal.md`, keep that file and fill it with the child template's guidance.
62:    Child scaffolding alone does not create its parent goal.
63: 4. Before filling the template, load [`authoring-standards.md`](references/authoring-standards.md) and [`goal-exemplars.md`](assets/goal-exemplars.md).
64:    Fill it with packet-specific content and apply both resources.
65:    Use three to seven self-contained completion criteria that can be checked without opening another file.
66:    Leave no template placeholders.
67:    Copy the criteria verbatim into the objective text required by the goal contract.
68: 5. For a phase parent, make the binding table match the filesystem. Add one row for each direct phase-child directory, with that child's goal document as the target. Keep the table only in the phase-parent goal.
69: 6. Keep the durable slice at or below 4,000 characters wherever the cap applies. Load [`references/budget-and-handoff.md`](references/budget-and-handoff.md): section 2 says which goals carry the cap and how to read the packet report, and section 3 is the cut order for a goal that runs over. Never remove a criterion or make one uncheckable.
70: 7. Before handing off any authored or revised goal, run `node .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-goal/scripts/check-goal.cjs <packet>` from the repository root and resolve each finding.
71:    A finding left open for any reason, an operator brief included, stops the run: report it, print no chat slice and end with `STATUS=FAIL`.
72:    To see which criteria may break rules 4 and 5 below, run the advisory lint `node .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-goal/scripts/lint-goal-criteria.cjs <packet>`.
73:    It always exits 0 and never blocks the handoff.
74: 8. Only after the checker passes, and after authoring or amending a parent goal, load [`references/budget-and-handoff.md`](references/budget-and-handoff.md) for the projection distinction and runtime matrix, then print its chat slice with `node .skilled/hooks/goal/bin/goal.cjs packet <packet> --workspace <root>`. The `chat_slice` is for the operator to set or resend. It is not a session bind.
75: 
76: ---
77: 
78: ## 4. RULES
79: 
80: ### ✅ ALWAYS
81: 
82: 1. Run the four pre-write decisions before changing a goal file.
83: 2. Derive each goal from the existing packet's source documents, not from a guessed or remembered summary.
84: 3. Start every goal from the asset template for its kind. Keep each template's fixed text identical to `goal.md.tmpl`. The parity test fails when they drift.
85: 4. Use three to seven self-contained criteria.
86: 5. Make each criterion checkable without opening another file.
87: 6. Remove every template placeholder.
88: 7. Preserve every criterion when cutting an over-budget parent.
89: 8. Compare each binding row with the direct phase-child directories on disk.
90: 9. Print the updated parent chat slice for the operator when parent goal content changes.
91: 
92: ### ⛔ NEVER
93: 
94: 1. Never change an asset template's fixed text or structure on its own. Change `goal.md.tmpl` through system-spec-kit, then carry its new fixed text into all three templates.
95: 2. Never modify system-spec-kit's template tooling or shared validator from this packet.
96: 3. Never bind a packet to a session, set or resend a session objective, inject runtime state or track whether an operator has set the goal.
97: 4. Never put a binding table in a top-level goal or a phase-child goal.
98: 5. Never omit a phase child from the parent's binding table or drop a completion criterion to meet the budget.
99: 
100: ### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
101: 
102: 1. The source documents disagree about a decision or criterion. They also must describe the same phase structure. Report any conflict instead of choosing a truth silently.
103: 2. A phase child is missing the source documents needed to author its goal.
104: 3. The parent phase map and child directories do not agree.
105: 4. A child change requires a parent decision or criterion amendment, but the request would leave the parent untouched.
106: 5. A parent cannot meet the durable budget without losing a criterion or making one unclear. Do not cut the criterion count. Ask whether the packet scope should be split.
107: 6. The request requires session-goal state or a change to a system-spec-kit-owned contract.
108: 
109: ---

126: ## 6. SUCCESS CRITERIA
127: 
128: - Every authored goal starts from the template for its kind, and all three templates match `goal.md.tmpl`.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?

681: 
682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |

134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

.skilled/hooks/goal/README.md:65:**Packet binding.** `bind <packet-path>` resolves the path inside the workspace, refuses anything outside it or without a `goal.md`, derives the objective slice (the pointer first, the binding sentence when the packet is phased, then the completion criteria copied out), which is never pasted in chat as section 4 of sk-create-goal's `references/budget-and-handoff.md` says, and stores the pointer. `resent` records the current durable-slice hash so the reminder stops; `resendPending` compares that hash with the file, and a log append or a reflow never changes it while a decision, binding row or criterion does. `log` appends one row to the packet's progress table under a per-packet lock, keyed on the packet's real path and held under the workspace's own state root, which deliberately ignores the record-store override: mutual exclusion over a shared file cannot depend on where each session keeps its private records, and honoring the override gives each session its own lock and loses rows, and refuses any write that would alter the durable slice, or any append to a document that is not valid UTF-8, which fails with `GOAL_NOT_UTF8` and leaves the bytes untouched; a CRLF document keeps CRLF. `unbind` drops the pointer and keeps the record. A text `set` carrying a new objective replaces the record and drops the pointer with it, because the session is then following the text you gave rather than a packet; re-setting the same objective refreshes in place and keeps the binding. `packet <path>` is a session-free read of a packet's slice, hash and size, and `packet-log <path> <item> | <state> | <evidence>` is the session-free append through the same lock, for a runtime with no management surface or a packet no session is bound to. Adapters append `renderResendReminder()` to the injection while the copy is behind: one line, never a block, naming the exact command on that runtime that records the resend (`/goal-pi resent`, `/goal-opencode resent`, or the scoped CLI line on Cursor and Devin). `show` reports `packet_state=bound|missing|unbound`, with a hint when the bound document is gone, and a text `set` past 4000 characters reports the truncation instead of clamping silently.

14: # Goal Authoring Standards
15: 
16: ## 1. OVERVIEW
17: 
18: The goal template defines the structure. These checks ask whether an authored goal states its purpose and records fixed choices. They also give a reader a way to judge completion. The [Human Voice Rules](../../sk-create-with-human-voice/references/hvr-rules.md) govern the prose.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 2. OBJECTIVE
23: 
24: Rule: Write one sentence that says what the packet exists to accomplish. State its purpose. Leave methods and progress out.
25: 
26: Failure it prevents: A template placeholder or work update does not tell the reader what the packet is for.
27: 
28: Reader check: Can you tell what the packet exists to accomplish from this sentence alone, without reading a method or progress report? Yes or no.
29: 
30: Example: "Produce ten iterations of evidence-cited research on a numbered, searchable commit grammar for sk-git, on how a per-commit identifier is minted without collisions across branches, and on how 9,106 commits are rewritten and their citations remapped safely." (`specs/sk-git/028-crawlable-commit-history/001-research/goal.md:43`)
31: 
32: ---
33: 
34: ## 3. DECISIONS
35: 
36: Rule: Record the frozen choices that later work must honor. State each so a reader can test work against it. Changing a choice requires an amendment.
37: 
38: Failure it prevents: Unstated or movable choices let later work drift without a visible decision to change.
39: 
40: Reader check: Can you test later work against each listed choice, and would changing one require an amendment? Yes or no.
41: 
42: Example: "This phase produces findings only. No file outside research/ changes." (`specs/sk-git/028-crawlable-commit-history/001-research/goal.md:53`)
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 4. COMPLETION CRITERIA
47: 
48: Rule: Write three to seven criteria. Each criterion resolves to one observable result. It may state a command's exit code or a count. It may instead name an artifact. Keep every criterion checkable without opening another file, then copy the criteria verbatim into the objective.
49: 
50: Failure it prevents: A vague criterion or a check that depends on another file leaves completion open. A count that conflicts with the declared scope gives two different completion targets.
51: 
52: Reader check: Does the goal contain three to seven self-contained criteria with an explicit result, and does the objective repeat them verbatim? Yes or no.
53: 
54: Example: "research/lineages/deepseek/deep-research-state.jsonl holds 10 iteration records" (`specs/sk-git/028-crawlable-commit-history/001-research/goal.md:75`). This criterion names an artifact and a count.
55: 
56: ---
57: 
58: ## 5. LOG
59: 
60: Rule: Record progress, evidence, deviations and findings only in the volatile log below the durable slice. Keep temporary status out of the objective, decisions and criteria.
61: 
62: Failure it prevents: Progress in the durable directive becomes stale as the work changes and can mislead a later reader about the packet's purpose or completion.
63: 
64: Reader check: Are all progress updates, evidence, deviations and findings below the log heading, with none in the durable directive? Yes or no.
65: 
66: Example: The progress row "| Phase opened | Pending | |" appears in the log (`specs/sk-git/028-crawlable-commit-history/001-research/goal.md:94`).
67: 
68: ---
69: 
70: ## 6. VOICE
71: 
72: Rule: Apply the Human Voice Rules to every sentence you author. Use plain, direct wording and support claims with specific evidence. Link to the voice standard instead of copying it here.
73: 
74: Failure it prevents: Vague or inflated prose hides what the packet requires and weakens the reader's ability to test its claims.
75: 
76: Reader check: Does each authored sentence read plainly under the Human Voice Rules, with claims backed by specific evidence? Yes or no.
77: 
78: Example: "This phase produces findings only. No file outside research/ changes." (`specs/sk-git/028-crawlable-commit-history/001-research/goal.md:53`)
79: 
80: ---

# Improvement Checklist

Ten rows decide whether a prompt needs work and how much, and the delivery rules decide what you see first.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

sk-prompt improves a prompt in one pass. It checks the prompt once against the rows selected by the effort level, writes from one component skeleton when an improvement is needed, checks the result against its stated success criteria, and delivers.

### When to Use

Use this reference when choosing an effort level, applying the checklist, or preparing a prompt for delivery.

### Core Principle

There are no rounds and no phases. The checklist is not a gate that repeats until clean. It is a single reading that decides what the prompt is missing before the prompt is written.

What that shape implies:

- A prompt that already covers the rows is returned early, without a rewrite.
- A prompt that misses rows is written once with those rows included.
- The finished draft is measured against its own success criteria one time.

# Improvement Checklist

Ten rows decide whether a prompt needs work and how much, and the delivery rules decide what you see first.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

sk-prompt improves a prompt in one pass. It checks the prompt once against the rows selected by the effort level, writes from one component skeleton when an improvement is needed, checks the result against its stated success criteria, and delivers.

### When to Use

Use this reference when choosing an effort level, applying the checklist, or preparing a prompt for delivery.

### Core Principle

There are no rounds and no phases. The checklist is not a gate that repeats until clean. It is a single reading that decides what the prompt is missing before the prompt is written.

What that shape implies:

- A prompt that already covers the rows is returned early, without a rewrite.
- A prompt that misses rows is written once with those rows included.
- The finished draft is measured against its own success criteria one time.

# Level Decision Matrix - Complexity Scoring Guide

Quick reference for selecting documentation levels (1-3+) based on LOC guidance and complexity factors.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

This matrix helps determine the appropriate documentation level for any task. Use it when:
- Starting a new spec folder and need to choose Level 1, 2, or 3
- Scope changes mid-implementation and level escalation may be needed
- Uncertain whether complexity/risk factors should override LOC guidance
- Coordinating a campaign that spans multiple phase folders or runtime families

### Usage

1. Check LOC estimate against thresholds (<100, 100-499, ≥500)
2. Evaluate secondary factors (complexity, risk, dependencies, testing needs)
3. If factors suggest higher level than LOC indicates, escalate
4. When in doubt, choose the higher level
5. Treat cross-phase coordination as a reason to escalate even when raw LOC stays modest

---

## 2. DECISION MATRIX TABLE (Progressive Enhancement)

| Level               | LOC Guidance     | Required Files                                                      | Adds To Previous                   | Use When                             |
| ------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| **1: Baseline**     | <100             | `spec.md` + `plan.md` + `tasks.md` + `implementation-summary.md`    | (foundation)                       | All features - minimum documentation |
| **2: Verification** | 100-499          | Level 1 + `acceptance-criteria.md`; verification checklist inside `tasks.md` | Closure criteria + QA checklist    | Needs systematic validation          |

147: ## 8. MANUAL TESTING PLAYBOOK
148: 
149: [`manual-testing-playbook/`](./manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md) holds nine deterministic operator scenarios in one category, goal authoring. Each scenario builds a disposable scratch packet, drives the mode against it and removes the scratch root when it ends, so a run leaves the repository untouched.
150: 
151: | Scenario file | Behavior under test |
152: |---|---|
153: | `top-level-goal.md` | A top-level packet gets its goal |
154: | `phase-parent-and-nested-child-goals.md` | A phase parent and its nested child goals |
155: | `add-goal-to-packet-without-goal.md` | The retrofit operation on a packet with no goal |
156: | `cut-over-budget-parent.md` | An over-budget parent is cut without losing a criterion |
157: | `refuse-leftover-placeholder.md` | The checker fails a goal that keeps template text |
158: | `detect-unbound-phase.md` | The checker fails a parent missing a binding row |
159: | `resend-parent-after-child-change.md` | A child change that amends the parent prints the updated slice |
160: | `route-session-goal-away.md` | A session-goal request writes no goal file |
161: | `lint-goal-criteria.md` | The advisory lint flags the criteria that break rules 4 and 5 and exits 0 |
162: 
163: The boundary cases carry the weight. In `route-session-goal-away.md` a run that writes nothing is the passing outcome. In `refuse-leftover-placeholder.md` and `detect-unbound-phase.md` the passing outcome is a failed goal check with the named finding, because the check catching the defect is the behavior under test. Every scenario run records a verdict, a reason and an evidence path under the sk-doc benchmark report tree.

167: ## 9. VERIFICATION
168:
